117	
118	   - `## Method` — queries run per source, providers called, errors/zero-hit notes,
119	     **and the access-preflight outcome** (which sources probed reachable, blocked, or
120	     partial, one line each with the probe evidence — a pointer to `access-report.json`).
121	   - `## Findings` — numbered `F1..Fn`. Every finding carries BOTH:
122	     - an attribution: `[docs-search: "Webhook delivery SLOs"]`,
123	       `[repo: git 4f2a91c]`, `[repo: lib/retry.ts:12]`, `[skill: queue-retries]`;

128	     - **Degraded-confidence tag (from the preflight).** A finding drawn from a source

132	       rests on a *critical* blocked/partial source MUST also drive a pending decision
133	       (below) so the plan gate surfaces it — proceeding on it silently is forbidden.

137	       behavior it alters.
138	     - **Consumers/callers**: who calls or depends on the touched surface —

140	       `lib/retry.ts` [repo: grep]" is an entry; "probably nobody" is a GUESS
141	       that must say so.
142	     - **Schemas & contracts**: DB schemas, API/request-response shapes, config
143	       keys, serialized formats the change adds/alters — and who reads them.
144	     - **Events/queues**: emitted or consumed events, topics, webhooks whose
145	       shape, timing, or volume the change affects.
146	     - **1-hop dependency neighbors**: the immediate upstream dependencies the
147	       changed code calls and the immediate downstream dependents that call it —
148	       one hop out from every touched unit, named explicitly (repo, service, or
149	       module), each with the evidence that put it on the list.
150	     An honest "blast radius unclear beyond X — could not trace consumers of Y"
151	     is allowed and becomes a pending decision if it blocks safe planning;
152	     an OMITTED blast-radius section fails the run. The plan stage sizes its
153	     rollout/testing against this map, and reviewers check the diff against it.
154	   - `## What could help that already exists` — MANDATORY, even if the honest content
155	     is "nothing found — searched X, Y, Z" (with the queries shown). List existing
156	     code/utils, org skills, prior PRs/commits solving similar problems, and relevant
157	     docs — each with a one-line "how it helps / why it might not fit".

160	     curator disposes: add the proposed answer to the finding, do NOT write an
161	     `answer` into decisions.json), `still open`, or `superseded` (explain). NEW
162	     questions surfaced by research get appended to `decisions.json` as pending
163	     `D-*` blocks with `"raised_by": "research"`.
164	   - `## Risks & gotchas` — sharp edges found (migrations, feature-flag interactions,
165	     load-bearing hacks), each attributed and confidence-tagged like a finding.

169	   unclear edges), the existing-help list, unknown disposition, and the
170	   **access-preflight summary** (sources reachable/blocked/partial, any blocked or

182	Brief: PROJ-2534, goal "failed webhook deliveries from notify-service are retried",

186	## Method

190

192	F1 KNOW [docs-search: "Delivery guarantees"] — org standard is at-least-once with
193	   capped retries + dead-letter for outbound calls; policy doc predates notify-service.
194	F2 KNOW [repo: lib/retry.ts:12] — exponential-backoff util already exists, used by 3
195	   callers (grep), configurable cap. Not currently used by the webhook sender.
196	F3 KNOW [repo: git 4f2a91c "add retry to email sender"] — closest precedent; touched
197	   sender, config schema, one alert rule, and 2 test files. Expect the same shape here.
198	F4 GUESS — timeouts are probably the dominant failure class (no metrics checked this
199	   run; would need delivery dashboards to KNOW).
200	
201	## Blast radius
202	Touched: src/sender.ts (retry wrap), config schema (new retry keys) [repo: F3 precedent].
203	Consumers: 2 callers of sender.deliver() — src/queue/worker.ts, src/api/replay.ts
204	  [repo: grep 'sender.deliver']; KNOW.
205	Schemas: config.schema.json gains retry keys; read by deploy tooling
206	  [repo: git log --follow config.schema.json]; KNOW.
207	Events: webhook.delivered event timing shifts under retries (was fire-and-forget)
208	  [repo: src/sender.ts:88]; KNOW. Volume to dead-letter queue: new — consumer unknown, GUESS.
209	1-hop neighbors: upstream — lib/retry.ts, queue lib; downstream — receiver endpoints
210	  (external), alerting rule on delivery latency [repo: 4f2a91c touched one alert rule]; KNOW.
211	Unclear: who consumes the dead-letter queue in prod — raised D-005.
212	
213	## What could help that already exists
214	- lib/retry.ts (F2) — reuse candidate; raised D-004 (reuse vs webhook-specific).
215	- Commit 4f2a91c (F3) — template for the file-touch list and test placement.
216	- Org skill `queue-retries` [skill-discovery] — includes the dead-letter runbook.
217	
218	## Unknowns after research
219	U1 resolved-pending-confirmation: F1 says org standard is capped + dead-letter —
220	   proposed answer recorded on D-001; awaiting human answer in curator.
221	U2 still open (D-002): repo has no failure-classification precedent; needs a human call.
222	
223	## Risks & gotchas
224	R1 KNOW [repo: src/sender.ts:88 comment] — sender deliberately fire-and-forget "to
225	   avoid blocking the queue"; adding retries changes queue latency (feeds the plan).
226	```

228	Wrong (each is a rejected output): a findings list that paraphrases the brief
229	("webhooks fail and should be retried" — restatement, zero new information); F1
230	without the doc citation (unattributed = GUESS at best, and unreviewable); marking F4
231	KNOW because it "seems obvious"; omitting the adr-index zero-hit note (silent provider
232	skip); an existing-help section left out because "nothing seemed relevant" (the
233	section is mandatory — show the searches); a blast-radius section that lists only the
234	files being edited (consumers, schemas, events, and 1-hop neighbors are the point —
235	the edited files are the trivial center); writing `"answer": "capped"` into D-001
236	(agents never answer gates).
237	
238	## Forbidden failure modes
239	
240	- **Ticket restatement**: research.md must be deletable-test-proof — if deleting a
241	  finding loses nothing the brief didn't already say, the finding was noise.
242	- **Unattributed findings / confidence inflation**: no citation → GUESS; KNOW is
243	  earned by a source you actually opened or a command you actually ran this run.
244	- **Silent provider skips**: every provider in stack.yaml appears in `## Method`,
245	  with hit counts or its error.
246	- **Proceeded on a blocked/partial critical source without surfacing it**: relying on
247	  a source (or its absence) that the preflight classified `blocked`/`partial` and whose
248	  criticality is `critical`, without an `access-report.json` record, a degraded-
249	  confidence tag on the dependent finding, AND a pending decision that carries it to the
250	  plan gate. Silently working around an inaccessible critical source is the failure this
251	  whole preflight exists to prevent.
252	- **Blast-radius omission or center-only blast radius**: no `## Blast radius`
253	  section, or one that lists only the edited files without consumers, schemas,
254	  events, and 1-hop neighbors — each with evidence.
255	- **Answering your own gates**: propose in research.md, never write `answer` fields.
256	- **Planning creep**: file-by-file implementation steps belong to the plan stage;
257	  research reports what exists and what's true, not what to type.

     - **Services/components touched**: the code units the change edits or whose
       behavior it alters.
     - **Consumers/callers**: who calls or depends on the touched surface —
       `grep`/`gh search code` hits, import graphs, API clients. "3 callers of
       `lib/retry.ts` [repo: grep]" is an entry; "probably nobody" is a GUESS
       that must say so.
     - **Schemas & contracts**: DB schemas, API/request-response shapes, config
       keys, serialized formats the change adds/alters — and who reads them.
     - **Events/queues**: emitted or consumed events, topics, webhooks whose
       shape, timing, or volume the change affects.
     - **1-hop dependency neighbors**: the immediate upstream dependencies the
       changed code calls and the immediate downstream dependents that call it —
       one hop out from every touched unit, named explicitly (repo, service, or
       module), each with the evidence that put it on the list.
     An honest "blast radius unclear beyond X — could not trace consumers of Y"
     is allowed and becomes a pending decision if it blocks safe planning;
     an OMITTED blast-radius section fails the run. The plan stage sizes its
     rollout/testing against this map, and reviewers check the diff against it.
   - `## What could help that already exists` — MANDATORY, even if the honest content
     is "nothing found — searched X, Y, Z" (with the queries shown). List existing
     code/utils, org skills, prior PRs/commits solving similar problems, and relevant
     docs — each with a one-line "how it helps / why it might not fit".
   - `## Unknowns after research` — for each U* from the brief: `resolved` (cite the
     finding; the human still confirms via the decision gate — research proposes,
     curator disposes: add the proposed answer to the finding, do NOT write an
     `answer` into decisions.json), `still open`, or `superseded` (explain). NEW
     questions surfaced by research get appended to `decisions.json` as pending
     `D-*` blocks with `"raised_by": "research"`.
   - `## Risks & gotchas` — sharp edges found (migrations, feature-flag interactions,
     load-bearing hacks), each attributed and confidence-tagged like a finding.

8. **Finish.** Set `research: done` (artifact `research.md`). Report: findings count
   (KNOW vs GUESS split), the blast-radius summary (touched units, consumer count,
   unclear edges), the existing-help list, unknown disposition, and the
   **access-preflight summary** (sources reachable/blocked/partial, any blocked or
   partial *critical* source flagged for the plan gate). Hand-off
   statement is fixed: research.md feeds the **plan** stage, and the plan's output
   MUST be rendered in **curator** — with all still-pending decisions shown as
   gates — before the intent check. Never start planning yourself.
   *Curator via subagents (CONTRACT.md):* any curator interaction this stage
   triggers (rendering pending `D-*` decisions, the open/poll loop) is delegated
   to a subagent — the main conversation receives only the distilled decisions
   and annotation summary, never poll JSON or server chatter.

## Worked micro-example

Brief: PROJ-2534, goal "failed webhook deliveries from notify-service are retried",
U1 retry policy, U2 definition of "failed". Abridged correct `research.md`:

```markdown

docs-search: "webhook retry", "delivery failure policy" (2 hits) | adr-index:
"webhook retry" (0 hits — noted) | skill-discovery: "notify-service", "queue retries"
(1 hit) | repo: git log --grep 'retry', grep -ri 'webhook' lib/ src/

## Findings
F1 KNOW [docs-search: "Delivery guarantees"] — org standard is at-least-once with
   capped retries + dead-letter for outbound calls; policy doc predates notify-service.
F2 KNOW [repo: lib/retry.ts:12] — exponential-backoff util already exists, used by 3
   callers (grep), configurable cap. Not currently used by the webhook sender.
F3 KNOW [repo: git 4f2a91c "add retry to email sender"] — closest precedent; touched
   sender, config schema, one alert rule, and 2 test files. Expect the same shape here.
F4 GUESS — timeouts are probably the dominant failure class (no metrics checked this
   run; would need delivery dashboards to KNOW).

## Blast radius
Touched: src/sender.ts (retry wrap), config schema (new retry keys) [repo: F3 precedent].
Consumers: 2 callers of sender.deliver() — src/queue/worker.ts, src/api/replay.ts
  [repo: grep 'sender.deliver']; KNOW.
Schemas: config.schema.json gains retry keys; read by deploy tooling
  [repo: git log --follow config.schema.json]; KNOW.
Events: webhook.delivered event timing shifts under retries (was fire-and-forget)
  [repo: src/sender.ts:88]; KNOW. Volume to dead-letter queue: new — consumer unknown, GUESS.
1-hop neighbors: upstream — lib/retry.ts, queue lib; downstream — receiver endpoints
  (external), alerting rule on delivery latency [repo: 4f2a91c touched one alert rule]; KNOW.
Unclear: who consumes the dead-letter queue in prod — raised D-005.

## What could help that already exists
- lib/retry.ts (F2) — reuse candidate; raised D-004 (reuse vs webhook-specific).
- Commit 4f2a91c (F3) — template for the file-touch list and test placement.
- Org skill `queue-retries` [skill-discovery] — includes the dead-letter runbook.

## Unknowns after research
U1 resolved-pending-confirmation: F1 says org standard is capped + dead-letter —
   proposed answer recorded on D-001; awaiting human answer in curator.
U2 still open (D-002): repo has no failure-classification precedent; needs a human call.

## Risks & gotchas
R1 KNOW [repo: src/sender.ts:88 comment] — sender deliberately fire-and-forget "to
   avoid blocking the queue"; adding retries changes queue latency (feeds the plan).
```

("webhooks fail and should be retried" — restatement, zero new information); F1
without the doc citation (unattributed = GUESS at best, and unreviewable); marking F4
KNOW because it "seems obvious"; omitting the adr-index zero-hit note (silent provider
skip); an existing-help section left out because "nothing seemed relevant" (the
section is mandatory — show the searches); a blast-radius section that lists only the
files being edited (consumers, schemas, events, and 1-hop neighbors are the point —
the edited files are the trivial center); writing `"answer": "capped"` into D-001
(agents never answer gates).

## Forbidden failure modes

- **Ticket restatement**: research.md must be deletable-test-proof — if deleting a
  finding loses nothing the brief didn't already say, the finding was noise.
- **Unattributed findings / confidence inflation**: no citation → GUESS; KNOW is
  earned by a source you actually opened or a command you actually ran this run.
- **Silent provider skips**: every provider in stack.yaml appears in `## Method`,
  with hit counts or its error.
- **Proceeded on a blocked/partial critical source without surfacing it**: relying on
  a source (or its absence) that the preflight classified `blocked`/`partial` and whose
  criticality is `critical`, without an `access-report.json` record, a degraded-
  confidence tag on the dependent finding, AND a pending decision that carries it to the
  plan gate. Silently working around an inaccessible critical source is the failure this
  whole preflight exists to prevent.
- **Blast-radius omission or center-only blast radius**: no `## Blast radius`
  section, or one that lists only the edited files without consumers, schemas,
  events, and 1-hop neighbors — each with evidence.
- **Answering your own gates**: propose in research.md, never write `answer` fields.
- **Planning creep**: file-by-file implementation steps belong to the plan stage;
